We have seen multiple reports about applications of Apple Vision Pro in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure using an innovative app on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, performed using the SportSuite Vision app, which brings "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." The content includes arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Below is Stryker's description of the app:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to view both physical objects and digital tools simultaneously in the operating room, such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. During arthroscopic surgery, surgeons typically rely on multiple displays in the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker stated that this is the first app authorized by the FDA for use with Vision Pro during surgery.
